title: cost-optimization-automation-batching-caching-quant-profiles-unit-econ-tooling
author: Maya Patel
description: Motivation: reduce per-token inference costs across hosted and dedicated deployments by shipping automated defaults and tooling that choose batching, prefix caching, and quantization profiles per-route and per-model. This PR implements a first-pass "autotune" pipeline that: 1) collects lightweight telemetry for latency/throughput/kv-hit-rate distributions, 2) proposes safe batching and caching defaults, 3) applies conservative INT8/FP16 quantization profiles where model validation passes, and 4) surfaces unit-economics impact in the Console and a new CLI report. The change set spans runtime heuristics, a background tuning service, Console wiring (UI + API), and unit-econ reporting. Checklist: - [x] telemetry collectors for sequence length, batch sizes, and KV cache hit ratios - [x] autotune service: analysis + candidate generation - [x] quantization profile runner and safety checks (per-model unit tests + regression eval harness) - [x] Console endpoint + UI summary for suggested defaults and estimated $/1M tokens - [x] CLI tool `rw autotune report` that exports route-level recommendations - [x] feature flag (autotune.enabled) and opt-out per-route - [x] e2e smoke tests and CI coverage - [x] docs and release notes Context: ENG-2314 and ENG-2401 tracked scope. This change is intentionally conservative: automated suggestions are non-destructive and require user confirmation in Console or the CLI. Quantization profiles are only suggested when the model passes a regression eval suite (sample prompts + metrics threshold). For Dedicated customers we expose separate recommended profiles that respect isolation/latency SLAs. Risk/migration notes: the existing per-route defaults remain unchanged until a suggestion is explicitly applied. Feature flag defaults to off for all customers; enabled for internal test orgs. Performance summary (canary): estimated median cost reduction ~17% on a mixed chat+completion workload (high variable seq len) with p50 latency change +5ms and p95 +28ms in the canary; customers can opt for stricter latency SLO enforcement which reduces gains. Follow-ups: - automatic rollout policy for A/B applying suggestions to a traffic slice - more aggressive quantization heuristics (INT8+KV-aware kernels) - integrate with billing exports for exact charge delta

release_notes:
- Add autotune pipeline to suggest batching, caching, and quantization defaults per-route and per-model.
- Console: UI and API surfaces for reviewing and applying suggestions.
- CLI: `rw autotune report` and `rw autotune apply` (requires confirmation).
- Unit-economics estimates (approx $/1M tokens) are shown alongside suggestions.
notes: This PR was rolled out behind feature flag and gradually applied to internal test orgs. Quantization suggestions require explicit user approval. Dedicated customers see separate suggested profiles that honor configured latency SLOs.
